clue.text: See 15
Pub requiring profit, say goodbye?

definitions.note: this definition works by sound: goodbye is said like 'good buy', which is what a cheap purchase is

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the counter in one
gain is a synonym for profit

explanation.surface: A drinker asks whether a pub that demands profit means farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to hear goodbye as 'good buy'; the question mark flags this playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A good buy is something purchased cheaply, which is exactly what a snip at the shops is called.

clue.text: Devil of a poet's on for the yellow fellow

parts.note: ..., the Greek epic poet, with the possessive kept as a letter
imps are little devils; the plural S is not separately clued, as the puzzle blog also notes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A demonic quality in some poet is offered as fitting a yellow-skinned man.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade needs IMPS but the clue prints the singular 'Devil', so one S is not clued; the blog flags the same gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon father in The Simpsons is drawn with famously yellow skin, so he is a fellow coloured yellow.

clue.text: Most distinguished head's taken over in case

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed over the next means it comes first

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
lest means in case, as in 'lest we forget'

explanation.surface: Someone eminent has had their leader removed inside a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word for highborn or grand, meaning finest or most illustrious.

clue.text: Fiddle with good seafood

parts.note: a fiddle is a swindle, a scam
pi is short for pious, so good

explanation.surface: A cheat involving fish dishes in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails served as a dish are a classic British seafood plate.

clue.text: Food in a tin has been forced out

indicators.note: out here means the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Canned grub that has been squeezed out of its container.
explanation.definitionFit: Salted beef sold compressed in a can is a staple tinned meat.

clue.text: Give ground feeding cow? Popcorn aficionado!

indicators.note: one piece feeds into another, going inside it

parts.note: a cow is something that moos, a mooer, hence the question mark

indicators.note: ground means crushed and reformed, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Give a cow some ground feed? Says the fan of popcorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow?' is a definition by example, a mooer; the question mark admits that. 'ground' gives VIEG and 'feeding' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes to the cinema is the typical fan of popcorn eaten during the film.

clue.text: Repeat a passage of writer, a teacher

indicators.note: passage of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A request to reproduce a section by an author who teaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To say or do again; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: The price for police security while you sleep, might you say, in compound?

indicators.note: might you say means the phrase is to be heard and spelt differently

parts.words: The price for police security while you sleep
parts.note: copper is slang for a policeman, and a night rate is the charge for overnight cover

explanation.surface: Wondering about the cost of having police guard you overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: COPPER NIGHT RATE is pronounced the same as the chemical name.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue salt of copper and nitric acid is a chemical compound.

clue.text: See 15
Commentary on work, as fine England football manager goes in front

indicators.note: goes in says the pieces before it go inside another piece

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship
OK means fine, all right
Don Revie managed England's football team in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A remark that one England football boss leads the way is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' looks like 'in front' but is the bow of a ship, the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A critical piece about a newly published title is a form of commentary on an author's work.

clue.text: Endless limitation for Scottish author

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter of the word it describes

parts.note: a barrier is a limit or obstacle

explanation.surface: A Scottish novelist whose restrictions never finish.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie, creator of Peter Pan, was a writer born in Kirriemuir, Scotland.

clue.text: Switch that is live feeding idea that's vulgar

indicators.note: one piece feeds into another, going inside it

parts.note: a plan is an idea or scheme

indicators.note: switch turns the pair of pieces round, so they are read backwards

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: An instruction to change something live that feeds a crude notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a noun but is an instruction to turn round EBEI, which 'feeding' sets inside the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian means of the common people, so coarse or lowbrow, a synonym of vulgar.

clue.text: Barking, a headless dog turns with a bark

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters go crazy and rearrange
headless removes the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A mad dog without its head spins around and barks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like a dog's noise but means mad; 'headless' leaves OG from dog, and the final A sits outside the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura is the aromatic bark of a South American tree, used for bitters.

clue.text: See 23
Difficult for me entering valley with deer to finish eventually in front

indicators.note: entering puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a combe is a short valley, a word common in English place names

indicators.note: difficult here suggests the letters are awkwardly arranged and need sorting

parts.note: a hind is a female deer

explanation.surface: A struggle into a valley alongside a deer ahead of the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult' rearranges FOR ME into EFROM, which 'entering' puts inside COMBE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a competitor trailing then overtaking to win at last.

clue.text: See 5
Gold variable in taste — here's aluminium ore

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the next

parts.note: a bite is a taste, a small mouthful
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
x is the usual algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A gold unknown inside a mouthful, presented as a source of aluminium.
explanation.definitionFit: Bauxite is the main mineral from which aluminium metal is extracted.

clue.text: Supreme singer remains captivating in a novel, Austen's first

indicators.note: captivating holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: dross is waste or leftover matter

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made fresh in a new order
first takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A singer's remains are enthralling in a novel, Austen's leading one.
explanation.walkthrough: The Supremes were a Motown group, so 'Supreme' is a capitalised member, not praise. 'novel' gives IAN, 'captivating' holds the result.
explanation.definitionFit: She was lead vocalist of the Motown group the Supremes.

clue.text: Unable to find coal then? English candidate

parts.note: with no mine there is nowhere to dig coal

explanation.surface: A coal hunter's failure leads to an English candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put forward for election or an award is a person nominated.

clue.text: See 2
See 22
Perhaps eight to nine American hospitals, where abroad, cutting rights

indicators.note: cutting means these pieces cut into the next one

parts.note: R is right, doubled for the plural
H is hospital, doubled for the plural
ou is the French word for where

explanation.surface: American hospitals somewhere overseas are slashing people's entitlements.
explanation.definitionFit: The busy commuting period, such as from eight to nine in the morning, is an example of peak traffic time.

clue.text: Chairman smothering me in fish, change for adulteress

indicators.note: smothering means wrapping round the following pieces

parts.note: Chairman Mao led China

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a dab is a flatfish
vary means to change

explanation.surface: A chairman covers me in fish, an exchange for an unfaithful wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Mao Zedong was known in the West as Chairman Mao. 'in' makes DAMEB, which 'smothering' wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's heroine Emma conducts affairs outside her marriage.

clue.text: Be stubborn while competing at tug-of-war?

definitions.meaning: refuse to give way in an argument
the pullers literally brace their feet into the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means resisting stubbornly, from planting the feet firmly to avoid being dragged.

clue.text: Cunning in people chasing long animal like a weasel

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind the piece it follows

parts.note: to pine is to long for something

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: men means people
art is craft or cunning

explanation.surface: Craftiness among folk who pursue desire.
explanation.definitionFit: The pine marten is a tree-dwelling mustelid, related to weasels.

clue.text: Cut hydrogen by itself?

parts.note: hydrogen is a gas
hydrogen itself is represented by its symbol H

explanation.surface: Reducing a substance to its element alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hydrogen' gives its type, then 'itself' gives its symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep cut or slash in the skin is a wound of that name.

clue.text: Eastern s-states in the papers

parts.note: S plus says, to state being to say

explanation.surface: A stammered report on eastern states in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Student essays are often called papers, as in term papers.

clue.text: Continue to write about northern flag

indicators.note: about goes round the following piece

parts.note: to pen on is to keep writing

explanation.surface: Keep writing about a northern banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow triangular banner, a kind of flag.
